### More California EV Owners Can Now Power Their Homes, Save on Energy Costs, and Support the Grid Through PG&E's Expanded Vehicle-to-Everything Program


August 24, 2026


*Bidirectional Energy and PowerFlex join PG&E's residential V2X program, helping accelerate adoption of new bidirectional technology and giving customers more ways to save money, boost home resilience, and support grid reliability*


*EVs from Kia, Volvo, Polestar, and Nissan are now approved and eligible for participation*


OAKLAND, Calif.


, Aug. 24, 2026


/PRNewswire/ -- Pacific Gas and Electric Company (PG&E) today announced a significant expansion of its Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) program, adding several new vehicles and charger options that give customers greater energy resilience and choice in how they power their lives and participate in California's clean energy future.


This includes the addition of Bidirectional Energy and PowerFlex as approved partners, broadening the network of automakers, charger manufacturers, and software solutions providers participating in the program.


**Q: What is PG&E announcing?** **A:** Today, PG&E announced a major expansion of its Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) program, adding new vehicles and charger options through partnerships with Bidirectional Energy and PowerFlex. This expanded network of automakers, chargers, and software solutions gives customers more choices, including the addition of Kia, Volvo, Polestar, and Nissan EVs *.*


**Q: Why is this expansion important for customers?** **A:** "This expansion is all about choice," said David Almeida, Director, Clean Energy Transportation at PG&E. "By broadening the mix of eligible vehicles and chargers, we're helping our customers access this valuable technology, while also offering them a way turn their EV into a home backup and a grid asset."


The expansion builds on the Ford, Tesla, Chevrolet, GMC, and Cadillac models already on the Eligible Products List.


**Q: What is Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X)?** **A:** V2X technology allows compatible electric vehicles to be used as mobile batteries. With a bidirectional charger, customers can use the electricity stored in their EV battery to:


- Provide backup power to their home during outages
- Help manage household energy costs
- Send power back to the grid during periods of high electricity demand
- Support overall grid reliability


PG&E's Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) program offers customers financial incentives to install new bidirectional EV charging technology, which allows a customer's EV to act as a mobile battery, capable of storing electricity that can be used to power their home.


**Q: What new options are being added to the program?** **A:** Customers can now participate through partnerships with Bidirectional Energy and PowerFlex. Newly eligible vehicle and charger combinations include:


- **Nissan Leaf (2018-2025)** with a **dcbel Ara** charger
- **Volvo EX90 (2025)** with a **dcbel Ara** charger
- **Polestar 3 (2025)** with a **dcbel Ara** charger
- **Kia EV9 (2024 and newer)** with a **Wallbox Quasar 2** charger
- **Kia EV6 (2025 and newer)** with a **Wallbox Quasar 2** charger


These offerings qualify for up to **$13,000 in additional incentives being made available through California Energy Commission grant funding** , subject to additional eligibility requirements.


**Q: Are there any other vehicles being added as part of this expansion of the program?** **A:** Yes. The expanded program also now includes new EV models from General Motors:


- Chevrolet Bolt (2027)
- Cadillac Celestiq (2025 and newer)
- Cadillac Escalade IQL (2025 and newer)


Customers can also participate through existing options from Ford, General Motors, and Tesla. Capabilities vary by vehicle and charger combination.


**Q: Has PG&E deployed V2X technology elsewhere?** **A:** Yes. PG&E has also advanced V2X solutions for commercial and fleet customers. The company has worked with school districts in **Fremont, Oakland, and San Francisco** to support the transition to bidirectionally capable electric school bus fleets. These projects help districts reduce emissions and operating costs while providing additional support for California's electrical grid.


**Q: What incentives are available for residential customers?** **A:** Residential incentives include:


- $2,500 upfront ($3,000 for customers in disadvantaged communities)
- $1,500 Early Adopter Incentive for the first 250 customers to enroll


**Q: What about commercial customers?** **A:** PG&E has supported Fremont, Oakland, and San Francisco school districts in transitioning to bidirectionally capable electric school bus fleets, helping the districts save money and reduce emissions. Today, over 90% of the nation's 500,000 school buses run on carbon-based fuels, releasing over 8.4 million tons of greenhouse gases annually, exposing students and communities to harmful fumes. By replacing gas - and diesel-powered vehicles with electric ones, PG&E is helping reduce tailpipe emissions and improving air quality.


Commercial incentives include:


- $2,500 upfront ($3,000 for customers in disadvantaged communities) for installing a
*3-phase bidirectional charger less than 50 kW.*
- $4,500 upfront ($5,000 for customers in disadvantaged communities) for installing a
*3-phase bidirectional charger greater than or equal to 50 kW.*


**Q: When can customers enroll?** **A:** Customers can enroll through June 30, 2027. To learn more and enroll, visit[Vehicle to Everything (V2X) Pilot Programs | PG&E](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4756029-1&h=2139070863&u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.pge.com%2Fen%2Fclean-energy%2Felectric-vehicles%2Fgetting-started-with-electric-vehicles%2Fvehicle-to-everything-v2x-pilot-programs.html&a=Vehicle+to+Everything+(V2X)+Pilot+Programs+%7C+PG%26E) .


**About PG&E**


Pacific Gas and Electric Company, a subsidiary of PG&E Corporation (NYSE: PCG), is a combined natural gas and electric utility serving more than 16 million people across 70,000 square miles in Northern and Central California. For more information, visit[www.pge.com](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4756029-1&h=1955834346&u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.pge.com%2F&a=www.pge.com) and[www.pge.com/about/newsroom](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4756029-1&h=2976105382&u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.pge.com%2Fen%2Fnewsroom.html&a=www.pge.com%2Fabout%2Fnewsroom) . **Media Line:** 415-973-5930


**About**[PowerFlex](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4756029-1&h=281375555&u=https%3A%2F%2Fpowerflex.webflow.io%2Fpge-v2x-pilot-program&a=PowerFlex)


PowerFlex, the largest installer of commercial solar in the U.S., is a clean technology solutions company making the transformation to carbon-free electrification and transportation possible. PowerFlex manages more than 70,000 EV chargers nationwide, making it the largest hardware agnostic EV charging provider in the U.S. It's backed by EDF power solutions North America, Manulife Investments and The Mobility House.


**About**[Bidirectional Energy](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4756029-1&h=2115567554&u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.bidirectional.energy%2F&a=Bidirectional+Energy)


Bidirectional Energy is a software company building the operating system for residential vehicle-to-grid (V2G) capabilities. Its platform connects EVs, bidirectional chargers and utility programs to help drivers lower energy costs, access backup power and earn income by supporting the grid—all while maintaining control over when and how their vehicles are used. Headquartered in San Francisco, Bidirectional Energy partners with automakers, charger manufacturers and utilities to bring bidirectional charging from pilot projects to broad adoption.
